deviations: None stopped the unit. Ancillary decisions, recorded and carried on from, per the deviation contract.

The guard's population is fence inputs and documented values, not 'every fence line the transcriptions copy'. A transcription restructures what it copies — the adopt fence's `if` becomes a ternary, the stream fence's reader loop becomes an assertion on collected categories — so a presence check over a restructured line cannot be written honestly. The title and the comment name the population they cover, so no gap sits between what the guard says and what it matches, and the report states the reasoning rather than recording a blind spot.

The claims list carries the two fence handler maps as multi-line strings with \n\t escapes. They are input literals the transcriptions reuse verbatim, so omitting them would have made the corrected title false again.

The U+2019 title is a double-quoted string rather than the escaped apostrophe or template literal the brief offered. oxfmt picks the quote needing fewer escapes, so an escaped single-quoted form would be rewritten on the next format run; the double-quoted form is the file's formatted fixpoint and matches the claim strings around it.

`npm run format` ran once to converge after the new claim strings landed. It reflowed the quoting of three claims and changed no string content; the non-mutating gates in § Gates were all run afterwards.

One presence-check limit is stated rather than closed: `guides/html.md:378` is byte-identical to `:345`, so one claim answers for both occurrences and an edit to either alone leaves the guard green. The transcriptions build the same page in each case, so the two fences are meant to stay identical.

Observation, not a criterion: the guard's population is a reading rather than a mechanism. Nothing recomputes it, so a fence that gains a documented value leaves the guard green until someone adds the claim. Deriving the claims from the guide would assert the guide against itself, which is why it stays a list; the completeness evidence is the assertion-by-assertion reading recorded in the report.
